alba.marta: The bakery opens at six even if the world ends.
alba.teresa: A letter for you, Don Piero. Came in the night, heaven knows how.
alba.piero: Don Piero reads the letter and turns grave.
alba.piero2: Clotilde thought of everything. Even of who would finish the lace.
alba.teresa2: Clotilde. Punctual to the very end.

hint.spinta: Look at the brass pins: they say where each one must be, and at what hour.
hint.indizio: A letter passes only to the one below: Teresa must be on top of Don Piero.

marta.testo: Keep Gino away from the Pier after nine. The water is high and he has no sense.

piero.testo: Dear Miss Ada, may my post reach me before ten, if the Lord and Teresa allow.

gino.testo: I WANT TO RING THE BELL!!! take me to chirch at 11

alba.bambina: On the Fondamenta they whisper it: the new lacemaker is just a girl.
alba.bambina2: Sixteen, dear. Sixteen! At sixteen I was already carrying the post.
alba.campana: At eleven the bell rings out of hours, out of tune and happy.
alba.campana2: Ah, Gino. Ego te absolvo, my son. But next time, gently.
alba.bagnato: Gino comes back from the Pier wet to the knees, with a crab in his pocket.
alba.bagnato2: Tomorrow I'll write it plainer, lacemaker.
alba.posta: Before ten. Thank you, my child. I'll put it with the others.
alba.brava2: Marta says it without looking up, her hands in the flour.
alba.posta2: The Lord and Teresa allowed it, Don Piero.

hint.spinta: Gino must cross someone every hour: make him run where he's needed.
hint.indizio: A letter can pass from Teresa to Gino, and from Gino to Don Piero.

margine.verso: Everyone has their way: some won't go under, some won't keep still.

perline.bambina: Rumour: “The new lacemaker is a child”

marta.testo: Gino is not to hear the gossip.

martaDura.testo: I wrote to you about the Pier. Now I write this, and only once: Gino is not to hear the gossip.

teresa.testo: Dear, Don Piero must hear the news before nine o'clock mass. It's only right the parish priest should know.

gino.testo: i want to go all the way round! Peer at 8, chirch at 11

alba.voce: The rumour goes round: “the little one weaves worse than the old one”.
alba.voce2: I only told those who asked, dear. Which is everyone.
alba.ginoSa: Everyone knows! The lacemaker's a kid! Bigger than me, though.
alba.ginoSa2: And who told you, Gino? No, don't tell me. I know.
alba.pieroSa: A child, says Teresa. So was Clotilde, when she began.
alba.giro: All the way round! Pier, Bakery, Square, Church! Tomorrow I'll do it backwards!
alba.fredda: Gossip, she says. Fine. That's fine.
alba.pieroSa2: Don Piero says it to the empty confessional, and to no one else.
alba.giro2: Marta searches the whole Fondamenta for him, still in her apron.

hint.spinta: A rumour passes both ways: whoever crosses someone who knows it, knows it.
hint.indizio: To keep Gino from the rumour, don't let him cross anyone who knows it.

nina.testo: Tomorrow I'm taking the nine o'clock ferry for the exam in Venice. Don't tell Dad a thing: he's at sea.

marta.testo: Nobody leaves today. I won't watch anyone go.

teresa.testo: I collect the post from the ferry. See that I'm at the Pier at ten.

teresaFredda.testo: Lacemaker. I collect the ferry post. At the Pier at ten. No gossip.

alba.ninaParte: Venice! If Dad asks, I was at yours, learning lace.
alba.ninaResta: The ferry left without me. The exam was today.
alba.ninaResta2: Nina stays on the Pier until the smoke is gone.
alba.nessuno: Nobody left. The sea remembers who leaves.
alba.posta: All the post, dear! And a postcard from Chioggia, unsigned. How odd.
alba.fredda2: Teresa counts the post without looking up. At the bottom, a postcard from Chioggia.
alba.ninaParte2: From the ferry Nina waves to the island with her book, like a handkerchief.
alba.nessuno2: Marta shuts the oven door harder than usual.

hint.spinta: At nine the ferry takes away whoever is at the Pier.
hint.indizio: Whoever must stay can't be at the Pier at nine. Whoever must leave must be.

nina.testo: I'd like to say goodbye to Dad before he takes the boat out.

bepi.testo: teresa not to go round telling about the net. specialy not my daughter

piero.testo: Let Bepi stop at the Church on his way back: he has a candle to light for his wife.

alba.barca: At seven Bepi's boat slips out from the Pier, into the fog.
alba.rete: You sold the good net. To pay for my exam.
alba.rete2: Nets can be made again. Daughters can't.
alba.candela: A candle for Elvira. Twelve years, today.
alba.candela2: Requiem aeternam. Stay as long as you like, Bepi. The church doesn't close.
alba.venezia: Venice. Mh. Your mother wanted to see Venice too.
alba.barca2: On the Pier a fisherman with no boat stays behind, watching the water.
alba.venezia2: Bepi says nothing more. He mends the net until evening.

hint.spinta: At seven Bepi takes the boat out: he must be at the Pier. He's back at eleven.
hint.indizio: From the Pier to the Church takes three hours: Bepi must move as soon as he's back.

perline.L_zeno: A letter for Zeno, from Chioggia. Signed “L.”

zeno.testo: The boy can come and see the lantern at twelve.

marta.testo: Gino is NOT to go to the Lighthouse. That mad old man is there.

teresa.testo: There's a letter for Zeno. It comes from Chioggia. See it gets there, dear.

alba.guardiano: Zeno climbs the Lighthouse stairs counting the steps, as every morning for forty years.
alba.calligrafia: This handwriting… no. It can't be.
alba.lanterna: From inside, the lantern is a sun! A sun that spins!
alba.vetri: The boy didn't come. I'd cleaned the glass specially.
alba.lontano: Away from that old man. It's for his own good.
alba.calligrafia2: Zeno folds the letter in four and puts it in his jacket, on the side of his heart.
alba.lanterna2: Mh. Now you know why I don't sleep.
alba.vetri2: The lantern turns all the same, for no one.
alba.lontano2: But Mum, the Lighthouse! The lantern!

hint.spinta: Zeno never strays more than two places from the Lighthouse.
hint.indizio: Gino can carry the letter to Zeno: he must be below when he receives it.

perline.L1: The letter from Venice for Nina: her exam result

nina.testo: The letter from Venice must reach me by 11. And the postwoman must not read it.

marta.testo: Today I don't want to see Teresa.

zeno.testo: The priest mustn't hear gossip about Nina: he'd tell her father.

alba.busta: The eight o'clock ferry brings an envelope with a Venice postmark.
alba.promossa: I passed! And nobody read it before me. Nobody!
alba.tuttiSanno: Everyone knew before I did. Even the mark.
alba.tuttiSanno2: Eight in Latin, dear! Well done! Oh… wasn't I meant to say?
alba.respiro: I didn't see her today. Easier to breathe.
alba.prete: Bepi, sit down. I've heard something about Nina, and I cannot keep it quiet.
alba.prete2: Venice. Mh. I've known since she learned to read.
alba.busta2: The sailor holds it like something too hot to touch.
alba.promossa2: Nina reads it ten times over, sitting on the wellhead.
alba.respiro2: Marta kneads in silence. For once the silence is light.

hint.spinta: The letter comes on the eight o'clock ferry: the sailor carries it.
hint.indizio: If Teresa holds a letter not hers at the end of an hour, she reads it.

teresa.testo: I want to confess. Let my burden reach Don Piero, and no one else.

nina.testo: What is Teresa hiding? I want to know. I'm seventeen, not seven.
nina.r1: Some things are better not known.
nina.r2: You're right: you're not a child.

zeno.testo: The boy should come by the Lighthouse at one. I promised him the lantern.

alba.cassetto: There are more and more envelopes in the drawer. I don't remember putting them there.
alba.confessione: Thirty years ago I read one of Marta's letters. In the Square. Out loud.
alba.confessione2: Ego te absolvo. But I'm not the one you should go to, Teresa.
alba.sempreSaputo: I know what you did, Teresa. I always knew.
alba.ninaSa: Teresa read one of Marta's letters, back in thirty-six. So that's why!
alba.lume: Zeno let me light the little lamp! Me! All by myself!
alba.cassetto2: Don Piero shuts the drawer. It barely closes.
alba.sempreSaputo2: Then why did you never tell me, Marta?
alba.ninaSa2: Nina writes it in her lined exercise book, then rubs it out.
alba.lume2: Mh. Put it out the way you lit it: gently.

hint.spinta: A secret only goes down: from the one on top to the one below.
hint.indizio: When Nina is on top, she also takes the secrets of whoever passes under her.

marta.testo: Tomorrow is my father's anniversary. Before eleven o'clock mass I want to speak to Don Piero, and I want Gino with me.

nina.testo: My enrolment form for Venice must go on the nine o'clock ferry. Give it to whoever boards.

zeno.testo: I didn't sleep last night. From three on I want to see no one.

alba.filoNero: At three in the night, at the lace's edge, a black thread crosses Zeno at the Lighthouse.
alba.anniversario: Twenty years today. Gino, cap off in front of Don Piero.
alba.partita: It's gone! The form has gone! Now it's real.
alba.scaduta: The ferry has gone and the form is still here. The deadline was today.
alba.insonne: I didn't sleep. Last night there was a light on the sea. A black one.
alba.anniversario2: Requiem aeternam. A stern man, your father. But he wanted you here.
alba.partita2: Nina runs along the Fondamenta without greeting anyone, so as not to cry.
alba.scaduta2: Nina puts the envelope back in her book, like a bookmark.
alba.insonne2: Zeno looks at the sea towards Chioggia, and says nothing more.

hint.spinta: The nine o'clock ferry takes whoever is at the Pier, with all they carry.
hint.indizio: Whoever boards the ferry must have the form: Nina hands it over from on top.

eco.ernesto: For Marta. Put it in her hand, Teresa. Hers alone.
eco.padre: Good morning, Don Anselmo. There's a stranger in the Square, have you seen him?
eco.quale: “Did you get my letter?” “What letter, Ernesto?”
eco.letta: “Come away with me, on the noon ferry.” That's what it says, I swear.
eco.nessunaParte: Here. Half the island has read it already. You're not going anywhere.
eco.anselmo: Teresa. What have you done, my child?

rivela.1: In '36 Grandmother sent Ernesto's letter through Teresa's hands, at market time.
rivela.2: Ernesto left alone, on the noon ferry. Marta stayed.

hint.spinta: Who is always in Church at eleven? Who leaves on the ferry? Who lights up?
hint.indizio: A letter passes to the one below. The father must know it before eleven.

eco.busta: Another envelope from Chioggia, Don Piero. You give it to Clotilde yourself.
eco.perLei: For the child. When the time comes, Zeno. Not before.
eco.campana: Three o'clock. I thought I heard the bell. It was the wind.
eco.onda: Did you see an old woman, out on the shallows? No? Then I dreamt her.

rivela.1: The ivory thread was Grandmother: the only night she wove herself into the lace.
rivela.2: Me? At two I was asleep. I don't know what thread you mean.

hint.spinta: The thread that breaks off at three belongs to none of the living.
hint.indizio: At two the ivory thread passes over the thread by the Lighthouse, and gives it something.

marta.noSotto: Marta never passes under Teresa. She told me with a “No.” that made the lace pillow shake.
marta.partenze: Marta watched the ferry leave and went back into the bakery without a word. Departures hurt her.
marta.padre: It was the anniversary of Marta's father. In Church, before mass, she held Gino by the hand.
marta.ernesto: In 1936 Marta wanted to leave with a sailor, Ernesto. Only he left.
marta.chi: Marta, the baker. At Grandmother's funeral she didn't cry: she left two loaves on the doorstep and went away.
marta.zeno: I wrote to Marta that Zeno isn't mad, he's lonely. She didn't answer. Maybe tomorrow.
marta.faro: I wrote to Marta “All right”. I don't know if I promised to keep Gino from the Lighthouse, or only that I'd heard her.
marta.comeVuoi: I wrote to Marta “As you wish”. I didn't ask her why. Perhaps that was just what she wanted.

teresa.luce: Teresa lit up. What did she see?
teresa.legge: If Teresa holds a letter that isn't hers at the end of an hour, she reads it. Not out of spite: letters keep her company.
teresa.cartolina: In the ferry post there was a postcard from Chioggia, unsigned. Teresa looked at it for a long time.
teresa.chi: Teresa, the postwoman. On the day of the funeral she brought me bread and told me the whole island while she was at it.
teresa.fredda: I wrote to Teresa that her news was gossip. Her next note was as cold as winter post.
teresa.amica: I said yes to Teresa. Now, when she passes under my window, she waves with her whole bag.

piero.pozzo: Don Piero takes everything and gives nothing. Letters not meant for him stay with him.
piero.buste: Don Piero keeps everything, even empty envelopes. He has a drawer that won't close any more.
piero.ascolta: Don Piero heard the rumour and repeated it to no one. Rumours stop with him.
piero.bepi: Don Piero found out Nina wants to leave, and told Bepi. Don Piero never lies.
piero.chi: Don Piero said mass for Grandmother in the voice of a man sleepy for forty years. He calls me “my child”.

gino.corre: Gino never keeps still. Every hour he must cross someone, if he possibly can.
gino.bagnato: Gino came back from the Pier wet to the knees. Marta wouldn't look me in the face.
gino.chiacchiere: Gino told everyone the lacemaker is a child. He added, on his own account: “A good one, though”.
gino.chi: Gino is Marta's son. He's eleven and can't keep still even in church.
gino.campana: At eleven Gino rang the bell. Out of tune, out of hours, happy. Don Piero laughed.
gino.promessa: I promised Gino the bell. Now it's a promise, and promises weigh more than notes.
gino.giro: Gino went all the way round: Pier, Bakery, Square, Church. Tomorrow, he says, he'll do it backwards.
gino.lume: Zeno let Gino light the little lamp at the Lighthouse. Gino talks of nothing else.
gino.chiede: I told Gino to ask Don Piero first. He answered with a drawing: a laughing bell.

zeno.faro: Zeno never strays more than two places from the Lighthouse. Like a dog on a chain, but with no chain.
zeno.insonne: Zeno hasn't slept for days. He says that at night, out on the sea, there's a black light.
zeno.nega: I asked Zeno about the night Grandmother died. He says at two he was asleep. He didn't look at me.
zeno.chi: Zeno, the lighthouse keeper. Grandmother called him “the keeper”, and nothing else. He called her “madam”.
zeno.riposo: Zeno spent the afternoon alone. He says he slept an hour, the first in days.

nina.curiosa: When Nina is on top, she takes as well as gives: the secrets of whoever passes under her.
nina.esamePerso: Nina missed the nine o'clock ferry, and the exam with it. There's another one in spring.
nina.tuttiSanno: The whole island knew Nina's exam result before she did. Teresa had read the letter.
nina.iscrizione: Nina's enrolment form didn't go. Today was the deadline. Nina says it doesn't matter. It matters.
nina.chi: Nina, Bepi's daughter. She reads as she walks and never trips. She wants to go to Venice.
nina.partita: Nina took the nine o'clock ferry for the exam. Bepi was at sea and knows nothing.
nina.dillo: I told Nina to tell her father. She didn't answer: Nina only answers when she's right.
nina.vai: I wrote to Nina: “Go. It's your life.” I wrote it, but it sounded like someone else's line.
nina.promossa: Nina passed, and she was the first to know. She read the letter ten times over, in the Square.
nina.iscritta: Nina's form went on the nine o'clock ferry. Now Venice knows Nina exists.
nina.abbraccio: I told Nina to hug her dad tight. She says Bepi won't let anyone hug him. He does, but he won't say so.
nina.delusa: I told Nina some things are better not known. She answered with two words of Latin: “Sapere aude.”
nina.grande: I told Nina she isn't a child. She underlined the sentence twice and sent it back to me.
nina.babbo: I asked Nina if her dad knows. She answered: “The sea knows. Dad, not yet.”
nina.partira: I wrote to Nina: “It'll go.” She copied it onto the first page of her exercise book, in capitals.

bepi.rete: Bepi sold his good net to pay for Nina's exam. Now Nina knows.
bepi.candela: Bepi lights a candle for his wife, Elvira. He says nothing. No need.
bepi.chi: Bepi, the fisherman. He greeted me with a nod, without a word. They say he's like that with everyone.

desiderio.nina: Nina wants to study in Venice and become a teacher. She says it the way you say a thing already done.
desiderio.gino: Gino wants to see the lantern lit from inside. He's written it three times, with three different mistakes.

libro.incrocio: Two threads that meet swap places. On the lace pillow as on the Fondamenta.
libro.spillo: Brass pins are not up for discussion. Until they're kept, the hour can't be fixed.
libro.sopraDa: “Who is on top, gives.” If the letter doesn't pass, I tap the crossing and flip it.
libro.voce: Rumours pass both ways. Once spoken, they don't come back.
libro.matassa: The skein is counted: each crossing, one arm's length of thread. Flipping costs nothing.
libro.molo: At boat time whoever is at the Pier goes away, with all they carry. Whoever arrives takes their place.
libro.segreto: Secrets only go down, from the one on top to the one below. Whoever confides them keeps them.

avorio.apre: On the lace pillow is Grandmother's last lace. An ivory thread belongs to nobody, and at three it is cut. Where to look: the chest, when it opens.
avorio.indizio1: The ivory thread passed over Zeno at two. It gave him something.
avorio.risposta: The ivory thread was Grandmother: the only time she wove herself into the lace.

martaTeresa.apre: Marta and Teresa haven't spoken in thirty years, Gino says. Nobody can say why, or nobody will.
martaTeresa.chiedilo: I asked Marta why she won't see Teresa. She answered: “Ask your grandmother.” Where to look: the Archive.
martaTeresa.confessione: Teresa has confessed: thirty years ago she read one of Marta's letters, in the Square.
martaTeresa.nina: Nina found out Teresa's burden: in '36 she read one of Marta's letters out loud.
martaTeresa.risposta: It was Grandmother who sent Ernesto's letter through Teresa, at market time. So that Marta would stay.

chiL.apre: The lagoon brought a bottle. Inside, a sheet: “My dear…” and a signature, L. Where to look: the bottles, every evening.
chiL.seppia: L. weaves on her own, in sepia black, because it doesn't show on blue velvet. Who taught her?
chiL.zeno: Zeno received a letter signed “L.”. He said: “It can't be.”
chiL.fuso: In the lighthouse-shaped bobbin Zeno lost, there is a carved initial: L.

pozzo.apre: Don Piero keeps everything. But what is in that drawer that won't close any more?

desideri.apre: Everyone wants something, and writes me only half of it. If I knew what everyone wants…

filoNero.apre: At three in the night, on the edge of the lace, a black thread crossed Zeno at the Lighthouse. I did not weave it.

lettere.bottiglie: The bottles come to the door in the evening, with the tide. The letters inside all begin “My dear”.
lettere.disordine: L.'s letters arrive out of order: one has been at sea ten years, another a month.

archivio.cassapanca: Grandmother's chest has opened. Inside, old laces rolled up, each with a ribbon and a date. Where to look: the Archive.
archivio.arc1: 1936. Grandmother sent Ernesto's letter through Teresa, at market time. In the margin: “So she would stay.”
archivio.arc2: Last night. The ivory thread breaks off at three. In the margin: “Just once, inside.”

lettere.L1: My dear, today in Chioggia there was a wind that would have made you laugh. I bought a lined exercise book, the kind I loved as a little girl. I don't know whether the bottles arrive. The letters, I'm sure, don't. L.
lettere.L2: My dear, today on the quay a little girl was counting the boats out loud, and she always went wrong at the same one: the red one. I thought that you, too, perhaps count things. I count the months. I don't tell you this for pity: it's just that numbers, from far away, are the only thing you can hold in your hand. I send you a hug in the shape of a bottle, which is the shape hugs come in here. L.
lettere.L3: My dear, I work in a net factory. We knot from morning to night, and the hands learn by themselves. Sometimes, without meaning to, I tie a knot my mother taught me, and the forewoman looks at me sideways: she says that knot won't hold. It holds, though. It has always held, even when you'd rather it didn't. I hope someone has taught you to tie knots, and to untie them too. The second is harder. L.
lettere.L4: My dear, I have learned to weave on my own. I don't know if that's the word: to weave without having the right. I use sepia black, because it doesn't show on blue velvet. Nobody taught me. L.
lettere.L5: My dear, today is your birthday, I think. I've lost count of the calendars, not of the birthdays. I bought a small cake and ate it on the quay, looking towards the island. You can't see it from here: there's always fog, or perhaps it's the distance. They'll have baked you sweet bread at the bakery. I remember it well: it was good even burnt, especially burnt. Happy birthday, from far away. L.
lettere.L6: My dear, last night I dreamt of the Lighthouse. There was a man on the stairs counting the steps, as he always did, and when he reached the top he started again from the bottom. I won't write his name: the sea opens the bottles, and the sea gossips. If you meet him, tell him I still remember the lighthouse-shaped bobbin. No, don't tell him anything. He wouldn't know who you meant. L.
lettere.L7: My dear, in Chioggia they say that when the sea gives back a bottle, whoever wrote it is about to return. I've thrown hundreds: I should have come back a hundred times over. Instead I'm here, at the window, writing. Tonight the sea is as black as my thread, and there's a wind blowing from your side. Don't be afraid of black. It's only a colour you can't see at night. L.
